paragraphs: Cyclomedia sells geospatial data built from street-level imagery, lidar point clouds, and aerial data covering public space. Public authorities are a core market, using it to manage streets, buildings, and public assets. Utility and energy providers use it to plan, inspect, and manage their networks.

Street Smart, the company's viewer, brings 360 degree imagery, lidar, and map layers into one browser-based workspace. From the desk, users measure distances along facades, pavements, and openings. Automated analysis detects pavement defects, surface types, and deterioration in high-resolution imagery. Property valuation is another stated use, supported by current visual evidence and measurements. Open integrations and APIs connect the data to existing GIS and asset management systems.

The company says it has worked in geospatial capture and visualisation for more than 40 years with public authorities across Europe and beyond. Specialised capture vehicles survey cities and regions throughout the year. Routes are coordinated with local authorities to limit disruption. Its case studies page lists a digital twin created for the London Borough of Harrow from street imagery and lidar.

quote.text: Shift more work from the field to the office by using Street Smart and work more efficiently.
